PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer — current state and blockers.

Context: This is a real implementation of the two-search-mode coverage optimizer (fixed-first and joint pair), not just the occlusion foundation. 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests were added. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs by bitset union and then applies quality/contribution tie-breakers; it is not greedy first-origin selection. Shared coarse-to-fine engine: 4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches. Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes.

Latest action: Aligned the runtime shader with the optimizer’s quality model. Replaced the old distance-only blend constant with angle/texel-density quality selection and explicit dominant-mode bias (blendMode 2/3 get 1.15 dominance). Removed the stale `projectedConfidence`/falloff assertion and replaced it with assertions guarding `projectedQualityAt` and the dominance-mode bias. Targeted regression in `tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts` passes (36 tests). Then ran the full suite plus lint and build: 42 test files, 371 tests passed; lint (tsc --noEmit) clean; build (vite) clean. Notable long tests: `projectionCoverage.test.ts` runs both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture (~39s); `projectedReceive.test.ts` and `projectedStyleCompile.test.ts` are real-WebGL pixel-readback/compile gates.

Current task intent (from user): Rebase onto main and resolve the PR conflict. Add an allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering. Run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100k+ optimizer integration test, not merely a BVH-construction test. Then spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that the goal is fully complete; report what is still lacking, fix it, and repeat until the subagent finds no holes.

Implementation decisions made: Keep the high-level two-mode design; the required fixes are implementation-scale and workflow correctness, not algorithm redesign.

Required fixes (still open, prioritized):
1. Replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance. Currently every non-floor scene object stores its entire AABB as an obstacle; candidates within 0.3 m of the AABB are rejected, and any point inside the AABB has zero clearance. For imported sets represented as one SceneObject whose AABB encloses the whole room, every sensible interior origin is rejected. Fix: candidate valid = camera sphere/capsule does not intersect nearby triangles, via the coverage BVH (point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast). Obstacle bounds should be per connected mesh or spatial cluster, not per imported set object. Add a regression test with one imported object containing a room floor, walls, and empty interior.
2. Replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with compact typed arrays and transferable buffers. Current representation expands every triangle into three independent Vec3 world-space arrays plus normals/IDs/area, then structured-clones into the worker, creating huge memory and GC pressure; the BVH recursively sorts/slices JS index arrays; raycasts allocate temporary 3-element arrays. For 3M triangles, minimum packed data is ~144 MB (positions 108 MB + normals 36 MB), and the actual JS representation is several times larger. Fix: `PackedCoverageGeometry` with `positions: Float32Array`, `indices: Uint32Array`, `normals?: Float32Array`, `meshRanges: Uint32Array`, `transforms: Float32Array`; transfer ArrayBuffers instead of cloning nested objects; for the BVH use three-mesh-bvh, a flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries; avoid expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle.
3. Move geometry extraction off the main thread. The panel synchronously calls `extractCoverageScene(project)` before creating/posting to the worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning still block the UI thread before the worker reports its first progress event. Fix: move extraction into the worker, or chunk it and yield between meshes.
4. Remove the ability to relocate existing panorama references. The UI/workspace handler writes optimized origins directly into the two existing panorama references via `updatePanoReference(primaryPanoId, { origin: originA })` and same for secondary. Changing metadata does not transform the already-rendered image; it projects old pixels from the wrong point and ruins alignment. Correct workflow: preserve existing panorama and its origin; for fixed-first, move the next capture origin to B, render a new graybox panorama, inpaint/generate the styled panorama, import it as the secondary, and associate each imported result with its actual origin; for joint mode, create a two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, import both, and associate each with its actual origin. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank. `reachableCoverage` uses the coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses a different fine sample bank generated with seed + 1. Those percentages are reported together and used for reachable efficiency, so the UI can show combined > reachable upper bound (clamp hides the impossible ratio but does not repair it). Also, for fixed-first the reachable set is calculated before the arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so the fixed first origin is not included in the reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use a common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first, include the fixed origin in the reachable union. Internal coarse/fine search banks can remain separate, but reported metrics must be evaluated on one shared final bank.
6. Enforce minimum separation in fixed-first mode. Joint mode rejects pairs below `minimumOriginSeparation`; fixed-first does not. `rankSecondOrigins` filters only by object identity, not position/distance, so even an identical candidate position can survive. Add `distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation`.
7. Reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below the candidate; local offsets retain the original Y, so on sloped terrain or multilevel sets an offset can move over a lower floor while preserving the upper floor’s camera height, leaving the origin floating above the new floor. For each offset: find the floor under the new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.

Important refinements (already identified, not yet fixed):
- The “four-level refinement” is not truly iterative. For every seed, all offsets are generated around the original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ± spacing/4, ± spacing/8, ± spacing/16). It does not select the best half-step result and then center the quarter-step search around that new result; it is still a useful multiresolution neighborhood sample, but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in the plan. A true refinement loop would update the center after every level.
- The optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. The optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; when both panoramas are visible, the actual shader blends them only by distance (now being corrected toward the optimizer’s quality model with winner-takes-most weighting via `pow(score, 4.0)` and dominance modes). The optimized coverage result and the visible result should fully agree; the shader should use the same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Recent patch moves this toward agreement but the alignment should be confirmed end to end.

Testing gaps (identified, not yet added):
- One large imported object containing an entire room.
- A 100k+ triangle performance fixture (the `projectionCoverage.test.ts` fixture covers this at the engine level, but the user explicitly wants a full optimizer integration test, not merely a BVH-construction test, plus a real complex imported-set benchmark).
- `reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage` invariant.
- Fixed-first candidate separation.
- Sloped and multilevel floors.
- Existing panorama origins remaining immutable.
- Candidate generation inside concave imported geometry.
- No GitHub Actions workflow runs are attached to the latest head, so the reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI.

The user wants a subagent-driven disprove/repair loop after the goal is reached; preserve that as the closing step, not a one-shot fix. Keep the required-fix list and testing-gap list as the active backlog.

Required fixes (still open, prioritized):
1. Replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance. Every non-floor scene object stores entire AABB as obstacle; candidates within 0.3 m of AABB rejected, any point inside AABB has zero clearance. For imported sets represented as one SceneObject whose AABB encloses whole room, every sensible interior origin rejected. Fix: candidate valid = camera sphere/capsule does not intersect nearby triangles via coverage BVH (point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast). Obstacle bounds per connected mesh or spatial cluster, not per imported set object. Add regression test with one imported object containing room floor, walls, empty interior. (Test added in projectionCoverage.test.ts: imported-room interior candidates via triangle clearance; imported room object retaining concave empty interior.)
2. Replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with compact typed arrays and transferable buffers. Current representation expands every triangle into three independent Vec3 world-space arrays plus normals/IDs/area, then structured-clones into worker, creating huge memory/GC pressure; BVH recursively sorts/slices JS index arrays; raycasts allocate temporary 3-element arrays. For 3M triangles, minimum packed data ~144 MB (positions 108 MB + normals 36 MB), actual JS representation several times larger. Fix: PackedCoverageGeometry with positions: Float32Array, indices: Uint32Array, normals?: Float32Array, meshRanges: Uint32Array, transforms: Float32Array; transfer ArrayBuffers instead of cloning nested objects; for BVH use three-mesh-bvh, flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries; avoid expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle.
3. Move geometry extraction off the main thread. Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, and structured cloning still block UI thread before worker reports first progress event. Fix: move extraction into worker, or chunk it and yield between meshes. (Partial progress: surfaceSampler.ts now chunks between meshes and yields, but extraction still runs on main thread before worker post.)
4. Remove ability to relocate existing panorama references. UI/workspace handler writes optimized origins directly into two existing panorama references via updatePanoReference(primaryPanoId, { origin: originA }) and same for secondary. Changing metadata does not transform already-rendered image; it projects old pixels from wrong point and ruins alignment. Correct workflow: preserve existing panorama and its origin; for fixed-first, move next capture origin to B, render new graybox panorama, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate each imported result with its actual origin; for joint mode, create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, import both, associate each with actual origin. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses different fine sample bank generated with seed + 1. Those percentages reported together and used for reachable efficiency, so UI can show combined > reachable upper bound (clamp hides impossible ratio but does not repair it). Also for fixed-first the reachable set is calculated before arbitrary first origin is evaluated, so fixed first origin not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union. Internal coarse/fine search banks can remain separate, but reported metrics must be evaluated on one shared final bank. (Test added: one fine validation bank for reachable metrics + fixed-first separation.)
6. Enforce minimum separation in fixed-first mode. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first does not. rankSecondOrigins filters only by object identity, not position/distance, so even identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation. (Test added: fixed-first separation >= 1.5.)
7. Reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor. Candidate validation only checks whether floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y, so on sloped terrain or multilevel sets an offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor's camera height, leaving origin floating above new floor. For each offset: find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance. (Test added: reproject local X/Z offsets onto nearest sloped or multilevel floor.)

Important refinements (already identified, not yet fixed):

True refinement loop would update center after every level.
- Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; when both panoramas visible, actual shader blends them only by distance (now being corrected toward optimizer's quality model with winner-takes-most weighting via pow(score, 4.0) and dominance modes). Optimized coverage result and visible result should fully agree; shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. Recent patch moves toward agreement but alignment should be confirmed end to end.
